import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 50

*References:*
* [erdosproblems.com/50](https://www.erdosproblems.com/50)
* [Er95] Erdős, Paul, Some of my favourite problems in number theory, combinatorics, and geometry.
Resenhas (1995), 165-186.
* [Sch38] Schoenberg, I. J. "On asymptotic distributions of arithmetical functions."
Transactions of the American Mathematical Society 39.2 (1936): 315-330.
-/

open Filter Set MeasureTheory Topology
open scoped Nat Topology

namespace Erdos50

/--
A function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is the asymptotic distribution function of the values
of $\varphi(n)/n$ if for all $c \in [0, 1]$, the natural density of $\{n : \varphi(n) < cn\}$
exists and equals $f(c)$.
-/
def IsDistributionOfPhiRatio (f : ℝ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ c ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, {n : ℕ | (φ n : ℝ) < c * n}.HasDensity (f c)

/--
A monotone function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is purely singular (or singular continuous)
if it is continuous and its derivative equals zero almost everywhere with respect to Lebesgue
measure.
-/
def IsPurelySingular (f : ℝ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  Continuous f ∧ ∀ᵐ x ∂volume, deriv f x = 0

/--
Schoenberg [Sch38] proved that the asymptotic distribution function of $\varphi(n)/n$ exists.
That is, for any $c \in [0, 1]$, the proportion of integers $n \le N$ satisfying $\varphi(n)/n < c$
approaches a limit as $N \to \infty$. This limit function is the cumulative distribution function
of the values of $\varphi(n)/n$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_50_schoenberg : ∃ f : ℝ → ℝ, IsDistributionOfPhiRatio f := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős [Er95] proved that the distribution function of $\varphi(n)/n$ is purely singular: it is
continuous, but its derivative is zero almost everywhere.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_50_singular (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hf : IsDistributionOfPhiRatio f) : IsPurelySingular f := by
  sorry

/--
Let $f$ be the asymptotic distribution function of $\varphi(n)/n$, so that for each $c \in [0,1]$,
$f(c)$ is the natural density of $\{n : \varphi(n) < cn\}$. Is it true that there is no $x$ such
that the derivative $f'(x)$ exists and is positive?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_50 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hf : IsDistributionOfPhiRatio f),
    ¬∃ x ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ∃ y > 0, HasDerivWithinAt f y (Icc 0 1) x := by
  sorry

end Erdos50

findings.description: The hypothesis constrains f only on [0,1], but IsPurelySingular f requires continuity and a.e. vanishing derivative on all of ℝ. This makes the theorem false for admissible extensions. Given any density witness f, define g(x)=f(x) for x≥0, g(x)=0 for x<−1, and g(x)=1 for −1≤x<0. Then IsDistributionOfPhiRatio g still holds, but g is discontinuous at −1, so IsPurelySingular g fails. The construction and the resulting conditional refutation of the universal statement were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean without sorry or reliance on any conjecture theorem. Schoenberg’s existence result supplies the required density witness.
findings.source_evidence: Erdős, Some of my Favourite Problems in Number Theory, Combinatorics, and Geometry (1995), p. 171, §9: the density of integers satisfying φ(n)/n<c exists for every 0≤c≤1, and “I proved that the distribution function is purely singular.” This concerns the density function on its stated interval, or its canonical distribution-function extension—not arbitrary values outside that interval. Original PDF: https://revistas.usp.br/resenhasimeusp/article/download/74798/78366/0 . The same statement appears at https://www.erdosproblems.com/50 .
findings.suggested_fix: Either strengthen IsDistributionOfPhiRatio to require the density equality for every c : ℝ, thereby forcing the canonical constant tails, or keep the current interval representation and replace the conclusion with: ContinuousOn f (Icc 0 1) ∧ ∀ᵐ x ∂volume.restrict (Icc (0 : ℝ) 1), HasDerivWithinAt f 0 (Icc 0 1) x.

reformulations.difference: The source asserts existence of the density separately for every c∈[0,1], while Lean asserts existence of a single real-valued function collecting those densities.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A function witness supplies each individual density. Conversely, classical choice selects a density for each point of [0,1]; extending the selected function arbitrarily outside the interval gives exactly IsDistributionOfPhiRatio. The equivalence is proved as Review50.schoenberg_form_equivalent in scratch.lean.

reformulations.difference: Lean quantifies over every real function satisfying the interval density condition, rather than referring to the source’s single density function on [0,1].
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Uniqueness of real limits makes any two witnesses equal on [0,1]. HasDerivWithinAt on that interval, at a point belonging to it, depends only on those interval values. Therefore the positive-derivative question is identical for every witness, despite unconstrained exterior values. Review50.universally_quantified_main_iff proves the equivalence with the question for any chosen density witness.

Schoenberg, On asymptotic distributions of arithmetical functions, Transactions of the AMS 39(2) (1936), 315–330, especially §2, Theorem 1 and §8: https://www.ams.org/journals/tran/1936-039-02/S0002-9947-1936-1501849-X/S0002-9947-1936-1501849-X.pdf — read through Jina’s PDF text representation.

review.notes: All five declarations were checked. The original 1995 paper explicitly says “finite positive derivative,” matching the real-valued derivative witness. Boundary checks proved f(0)=0, f(1)=1, the interval range bounds and monotonicity; small finite counts were also tested. The completed scratch file compiles successfully, and the counterexample and equivalence proofs have no sorryAx dependencies. The current source still marks the main problem OPEN, while recording the background results as established; no status discrepancy was found.

submission.summary: Restricted the singularity conclusion to [0,1], using ContinuousOn and an almost-everywhere HasDerivWithinAt statement with Lebesgue measure restricted to the interval. Updated the theorem’s docstring and left all other declarations and attributes unchanged. The required compilation succeeds with only the expected `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings.
